subject: POC plan: model selection & eval criteria for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: POC plan: model selection & eval criteria for Acme Retail

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Great to meet you on the call today. Thanks for walking through the Acme Retail use case and sharing the high-level goals. As promised, here’s a concise recap and a proposed POC plan so we can align on success criteria, timelines, and ownership.

Summary of goals (from today)
- Replace rule-based keyword search in customer support routing with a model-powered intent classifier + reranking to improve correct routing for multilingual tickets.
- Baseline metrics you care about: Intent classification accuracy (macro F1), routing precision/recall, and latency (p95) for end-to-end inference.
- Additional requirements: Spanish and Portuguese support for transcripts, PII-safe handling, and quantized model footprint for lower cost.

Proposed POC scope (4-week timeline)
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff, NDA/procurement checkpoints, dataset handoff (sample_prompts.csv).
- Week 1: Environment & model provisioning, baseline (rule-based) metrics capture.
- Week 2: Prompt engineering and eval harness run on primary model + fallback variant. Collect accuracy/latency metrics.
- Week 3: Iterate on prompts, add simple reranking layer, run multi-language tests.
- Week 4: Final metrics, executive summary, and next-step recommendation (Dedicated vs Hosted).

Success criteria (suggested)
- Intent macro F1 >= 0.85 on your validation set OR >= 15% relative improvement over rule baseline.
- Routing precision >= 0.90 and routing recall >= 0.80.
- End-to-end p95 latency <= 250 ms for single-request path (with our proposed batching off for low-latency flows).
- Hallucination/incorrect-routing rate < 5% on sampled live tickets.

Model selection for trial
- Primary model (recommended): Llama-2-13b-chat (HF weights, CPU/GPU quantized variant) — chosen for strong instruction-following and good multi-lingual capability when prompted.
- Fallback model: Llama-2-7b-chat (lower-cost quantized variant) — used as an A/B or fallback path if 13B exceeds latency/cost targets.
- Multilingual handling: We'll evaluate prompts and small instruction templates for Spanish/Portuguese. If we see large gaps, we can test a multilingual model (e.g., Mistral / Bloomz family) as an additional probe.

Data & security notes
- For the POC we only need a de-identified sample (200-500 rows) with language tag and expected routing label. Please avoid sending full PII until we have an NDA and KMS in place.

Next steps / ownership
- Action for Acme: Share sample_prompts.csv, confirm timeline (preferred start date), and any procurement/NDA blockers.
- Action for Redwood: Rishi to spin up eval harness and model variants; Dev to provision a private trial environment and attach logging; Naomi to coordinate success-metric tracking and CS handover.

If this looks good I’ll queue the kickoff and we can lock a start date next week.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acmeretail.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC plan: model selection & eval criteria for Acme Retail

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful and aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset: We can provide a 300-row de-identified sample with language labels by Thursday. We'll include English/Spanish/Portuguese examples.
2) NDA/procurement: Legal will need an NDA before we share anything with PII; we can share the de-identified sample without NDA.
3) Multilingual: Spanish is priority; Portuguese optional but nice-to-have. If the Llama-2-13b approach requires heavy tuning for Spanish, are you able to run a comparison against a Spanish-optimized model (if you recommend one)?
4) Cost/latency: Our initial throughput target is modest (50 req/s) but latency is important — 250 ms p95 is our target.

We have availability to start the POC next Monday (Mar 16). Please loop in any SEs we need now.

- Jordan
Head of Customer Experience | Acme Retail
jordan.hayes@acmeretail.com

Subject: FW: POC plan: model selection & eval criteria for Acme Retail

Team — looping you in with the customer confirmation and dataset timeline. Jordan said they can start the week of Mar 16. Please see the asks below and confirm you can hit these dates.

Rishi: Can you prep two model variants in our trial environment (llama-2-13b-chat quantized, llama-2-7b-chat quantized) and a simple eval harness that computes macro F1, precision/recall, and p95 latency? We should include a Spanish/Portuguese language split in the evaluation. Aim to have a baseline run completed by EOD Mar 18.

Dev: Please provision an isolated trial environment (VPC) with logging and token-level cost/latency tracing. Keep the environment accessible to customer via a restricted API key. If possible, enable low-latency path (no batching) and a cost-aware path (batched) so we can demonstrate both.

Naomi: Can you own success-metric tracking and the final executive summary? Draft the measurement sheet and reporting cadence (weekly).

Notes: If Llama-2-13b shows poor Spanish behavior in the baseline, we can run a quick probe with Bloomz-7b or a Spanish-centric model — coordinate with Rishi on which additional model to pull.

Thanks —
Marissa
